facts: Consolidated revenue for Q1 fiscal 2026 decreased by 11.1%, with the Consumer Floral and Gift segment declining 14.6% and Gourmet Foods and Gift Baskets declining 8.6%.
First quarter gross margin decreased 240 basis points to 35.7% from 38.1% in the prior year period, primarily due to sales deleveraging and higher tariffs.
Adjusted EBITDA loss for Q1 was $32.9 million compared to a loss of $27.9 million in the prior year period.
After adjusting for timing-related items, Q1 represented the first year-over-year improvement in adjusted EBITDA trends over the past 7 quarters.
The company has already implemented $17 million in annualized cost reductions and anticipates achieving an incremental $50 million in cost savings over the next 2 years on a run rate basis.
Of the anticipated $50 million in cost savings, management expects half to be realized in fiscal 2026 and the remaining half in fiscal 2027.
Net debt increased to $259.3 million from $224.1 million a year ago, with $157 million in term debt and $110 million in revolving credit facility borrowings.
Wholesale order timing shifted approximately $3-4 million in revenue from Q1 to Q2 compared to the prior year.
The company is now selling products through third-party marketplaces including Amazon and walmart.com, with early traction described as positive.
Colombia represents approximately 60-70% of fresh flowers imported into the U.S., making potential tariffs on Colombian imports a significant risk to the floral industry.
Q3 2025 revenue was $851.6 million, representing a 4.4% increase over Q3 2024, while adjusted EBITDA declined to $173 million from $194.3 million in the prior year period.
The company reduced its 2025 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $650-$660 million from the prior range of $675-$700 million.
Same-facility volume growth was 1.3% in Q3, approximately 100 basis points below internal expectations.
Capital expenditures in 2026 are expected to be at least $300 million lower than the revised 2025 CapEx guidance of $610-$630 million.
The company expects to generate positive adjusted free cash flow for full year 2026, a milestone previously expected to reach only on a run rate basis exiting 2026.
Acadia added over 1,700 beds across 2024 and 2025 year-to-date and expects to add 500-700 beds in 2026.
The company ceased operations at 5 facilities during Q3 that no longer aligned with strategic priorities or demonstrated persistent underperformance.
Government investigation-related costs were $39 million in Q3, down 28% from Q2, with further moderation expected in Q4.
Up to $22 million of additional adjusted EBITDA from supplemental payments awaiting CMS approval is not included in 2025 outlook due to timing uncertainty.
632 new beds will enter the same-facility calculation in Q1 2026, expected to contribute meaningfully to volume and EBITDA growth.
Rackspace exceeded Q4 revenue guidance with total GAAP revenue of $683 million, driven by public cloud outperformance.
Q4 non-GAAP operating profit was $41 million, above the high end of guidance, with margins up 120 basis points sequentially to 6% of GAAP revenue.
Non-GAAP loss per share was $0.01 in Q4, beating the guided range of a $0.03 to $0.05 loss per share.
Full year 2025 free cash flow was $91 million, with the company ending the year with $106 million in cash and $397 million in total liquidity.
Private cloud Q4 revenue of $241 million came in below guided range due to a health care contract ramping more slowly than expected, which is now expected to begin ramping in Q2 2026.
Public cloud Q4 revenue of $442 million exceeded the guided range, with services revenue growing 28% year-over-year in the quarter and 6% for the full year.
For fiscal 2026, Rackspace expects total GAAP revenue of $2.6 billion to $2.7 billion (down 1% YoY at midpoint), with private cloud revenue up 6% YoY and public cloud revenue down 6% YoY at midpoint.

Full year 2026 non-GAAP operating profit is expected to be $160 million to $170 million, representing growth of 31% at the midpoint, while adjusted EBITDA is expected to be $305 million to $315 million, up 12% at the midpoint.
Excluding the planned transition of a large low-margin government contract, public cloud services revenue is expected to grow mid- to high teens in 2026.
Rackspace currently has 30 Palantir-trained platform engineers and plans to scale to over 250 within the next 12 months as part of its AI platform engineering growth strategy.

The company estimates the annualized gross pre-mitigation impact of higher tariffs to be in the range of $200 million to $250 million, with the net impact on 2025 operating income estimated at $25 million to $35 million.
The company has identified $45 million in gross savings for 2026, with approximately $35 million coming from a planned 15% reduction in office-based roles by year-end 2025.
Third quarter adjusted earnings per share were $0.74 compared to $1.64 in the prior year period.
U.S. Retail comparable sales increased 2% in the third quarter, marking the second consecutive quarter of positive comp growth, with average unit retail prices up mid-single digits.
Quarter-to-date U.S. Retail comparable sales in Q4 are up approximately 7%.
The company's effective duty rate has increased to the high 30% range versus approximately 13% historically.
The company is targeting 150 North America store closures, with up to 100 expected to close by the end of 2026, representing approximately $110 million in trailing twelve-month revenue.
Net inventories increased 8% versus last year to $656 million, with approximately $34 million of the increase attributable to higher tariffs.
The company has received commitments from bank group members for a new 5-year $750 million credit facility expected to be in place in the coming weeks.

Management stated on a preliminary basis they are planning for growth in both sales and earnings in 2026, with sales growth planned higher than a typical year given price increases in response to tariffs.
Total revenue increased 47% year-over-year to $23.5 million in Q3 2025, with Irwin Naturals contributing $6.8 million of the $7.5 million revenue increase.
Gross margin declined to 37.2% in Q3 2025 from 43.8% in Q3 2024, or 38.9% excluding the $0.4 million inventory step-up amortization from the Irwin acquisition.
Net income decreased to $0.9 million in Q3 2025 from $2.1 million in Q3 2024, primarily due to elevated M&A expenses, lower gross margin, and higher income tax expense.
MusclePharm delivered 55% organic revenue growth in Q3 2025, with wholesale revenue increasing 112%, while gross margin declined to 19.8% due to rising whey protein costs.
Whey protein costs have risen from $3-4 per pound to $6.30 per pound for Q1 2026 supply, with Q2 2026 pricing starting at $7 per pound, prompting planned January 1 price increases.
Irwin Naturals Amazon sales, which began October 11, are currently generating approximately $10,000 daily (~$3.6 million annualized) with only 116 of 242 product listings actively selling.
Amazon subscriber counts began declining in September 2025 for the first time in seven years across all brands except MRC, with company noting across-the-board consumer weakness.
Approximately $650,000 of remaining inventory step-up amortization from the Irwin acquisition will flow through in Q4 2025, after which reported numbers will be clean.
The company's term loan balance begins amortizing at the end of December, with debt reduction expected in Q4 and beyond after using Q3 cash flow for Irwin acquisition expenses.
Consumer confidence, as measured by the University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Index, is close to its lowest level since tracking began in 1951, contributing to softer October revenue.

Full year 2025 total product sales were $28.9 billion, exceeding the guidance range of $28.4 billion to $28.7 billion, with base business sales (excluding Veklury) of $28 billion surpassing the $27.4 billion to $27.7 billion guidance range.
The HIV business grew 6% year-over-year to $20.8 billion in 2025, but excluding an estimated $900 million headwind from Part D redesign, underlying HIV growth was 10%.
Yeztugo full year 2025 sales were $150 million, with the company guiding to approximately $800 million in 2026 revenue and achieving 90% payer coverage well ahead of its 1-year target.
Full year 2025 non-GAAP diluted EPS was $8.15, and the company guided 2026 non-GAAP diluted EPS to $8.45 to $8.85 per share.
The company expects 2026 total product sales between $29.6 billion and $30 billion, with base business sales of $29 billion to $29.4 billion representing 4% to 5% growth over 2025.
Cell therapy sales were $1.8 billion in 2025, down 7% year-over-year, and the company expects Kite revenue to decline approximately 10% in 2026 due to continued competitive headwinds.
Livdelzi grew 42% sequentially in Q4 to $150 million, achieving more than 50% U.S. market share in second-line PBC, aided by a competitor product withdrawal.

Trodelvy full year 2025 sales grew 6% to $1.4 billion, with the first-line metastatic triple-negative breast cancer opportunity estimated at approximately 10,000 women and roughly double the current second-line addressable population.

The company returned $5.9 billion to shareholders in 2025, representing approximately 63% of free cash flow, including $1.9 billion in share repurchases, and committed to returning at least 50% of free cash flow on average.

Gilead expects an approximate 2% headwind to 2026 HIV growth from a U.S. government drug pricing agreement and proposed Affordable Care Act changes, noting that absent these headwinds, full year base business growth would be 6% to 7%.

Q1 2026 sales were $762 million (down 4% YoY, +1% like-for-like ex-India) and beat the guidance midpoint by $12 million, while Q1 adjusted EBITDA of $72 million exceeded the high end of guidance by $17 million and adjusted EPS loss of $0.23 was $0.15 better than midpoint.

Q2 2026 guidance calls for revenue of $850M–$900M (down 17% at midpoint, almost entirely from lower diamide partner sales and India removal), EBITDA of $130M–$150M (down 32%), and adjusted EPS of $0.16–$0.26 (down 70% at midpoint).

Full-year 2026 guidance was maintained at sales of $3.6B–$3.8B, EBITDA of $670M–$730M (-17% at midpoint), and adjusted EPS of $1.63–$1.89 (-41% at midpoint), with Iran-related cost pressures assumed to roughly offset tariff-related benefits.

FMC is targeting approximately $1 billion of debt paydown in 2026, with line of sight to ~$700 million (70%) already in active negotiation, including the India commercial business sale (expected to sign in May), a new AI licensing deal with upfront payment (closing in weeks), noncore molecule sales, and sale-leaseback real estate deals.

Rynaxypyr total sales are forecast to decline from ~$800M in 2025 to ~$700M in 2026, with branded sales flat at $600M but partner sales falling from $200M to under $100M, while branded earnings are expected to remain flat.

Q1 sales of new active ingredients (Isoflex, fluindapyr, Dodhylex) doubled year-over-year, and Isoflex active received EU regulatory approval—the first new herbicide approved in the EU since 2019—providing access to more than 55 million planted hectares.

Gross debt ended Q1 at ~$4.5 billion (up $459M from year-end), with gross debt to TTM EBITDA at 5.7x and net debt to EBITDA at 5.2x; the revolver was amended on April 16 to become fully secured with ~$6B in direct liens collateral, waiving the total leverage covenant until December 31, 2026, when it will be reinstated at 6.75x.
FMC intends to issue a secured high-yield bond this quarter to redeem $500 million of notes maturing in October, with full year 2026 interest expense expected at $255M–$275M (up ~$25M YoY).

By end of April, FMC had orders representing 32% of H2 direct sales in Brazil, with ~50% expected by end of June—a higher percentage on a higher sales target than last year—supporting the H2 bridge of ~$425M sales improvement over H1 (non-diamide core +$150–200M, Rynaxypyr +$50–80M, new AIs +$175–200M).

Q1 free cash flow was negative $628 million ($32M worse than prior year), with full-year 2026 free cash flow guided to negative $65M to positive $65M, including ~$150 million in restructuring cash spending, with management expecting H1 2026 to be the earnings trough and improved results in 2027 and 2028.
Avery Dennison delivered Q3 adjusted EPS of $2.37, up 2% year-over-year and above the midpoint of expectations.
Q3 adjusted EBITDA margin was 16.5%, up 10 basis points compared to prior year.
The company generated adjusted free cash flow of nearly $270 million in Q3 with a net debt to adjusted EBITDA ratio of 2.2.

Year-to-date, the company repurchased approximately $454 million in stock and grew its dividend by 7%, returning roughly $670 million to shareholders through repurchases and dividends in the first 9 months.

Avery Dennison announced a major partnership with Walmart to deploy RFID solutions in fresh grocery categories (bakery, meat, and deli), which management estimates could drive high single-digit to low double-digit growth on total 2025 enterprise Intelligent Labels revenue over a 2-year rollout period.
High-value categories now represent 45% of total business year-to-date, an increase compared to prior year.
Enterprise-wide Intelligent Labels sales grew approximately 3% compared to prior year, with food, logistics, and industrial categories combined up mid-single digits.
Materials Group adjusted EBITDA margin was 17.5% in Q3, up 50 basis points year-over-year, driven by productivity and modest volume mix growth.
Q4 guidance calls for reported sales growth of 5% to 7% and adjusted EPS of $2.35 to $2.45, with organic growth expected at 0% to 2%.
The company closed the $390 million Taylor Adhesives acquisition and issued a EUR 500 million note to fund it, with full-year interest expense now expected to be approximately $135 million.
Sales increased 3% organically year-over-year, marking the company's first quarter of organic growth in 2 years after 8 quarters of broad market weakness.
Adjusted EPS increased to $0.34 compared to $0.29 in the prior year quarter, while adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 15.3% from 14.3%.
The company raised its FY26 sales outlook to $2.1 billion to $2.17 billion and adjusted EPS outlook to $1.35 to $1.65.
The company realized $8 million in restructuring savings this quarter and remains on track for $35 million in total restructuring savings for the year.
Aerospace and Defense sales grew 20% on a constant currency basis, driven by improved build rates and easing supply chain pressures.
Free operating cash flow decreased to negative $5 million from positive $21 million in the prior year, primarily due to higher inventory investment from rising tungsten prices.
The company returned $25 million to shareholders through $10 million in share repurchases (475,000 shares) and $15 million in dividends.
Net price and tariff surcharge combined is expected to contribute approximately 7% to FY26 sales, up from the prior outlook of approximately 4%.
The Power Generation market represents a $250 million total addressable market that is projected to grow at a 10% CAGR over the next few years.
The company maintained combined cash and revolver availability of approximately $800 million with no near-term debt refunding requirements.
Q2 FY26 adjusted EPS from continuing operations was $0.60 versus $0.69 a year ago (with a $0.04 FX headwind), while GAAP diluted EPS fell to $0.09 from $0.43.

Organic net sales declined 240 basis points in the quarter, with North America down 4.8% (Sun Care down ~10%) and International up 1%, while U.S. value share rose ~50 bps with gains across branded manual shave, shave preps, Grooming, Sun Care and Skin Care.
Adjusted gross margin fell 310 bps as 220 bps of productivity savings were offset by 420 bps of core inflation and tariffs, 70 bps of unfavorable mix/promo net of pricing, and 40 bps of FX.
Management reaffirmed FY26 guidance: organic net sales down 1% to up 2%, adjusted EPS of $1.70–$2.10, adjusted EBITDA of $245–$265 million, and adjusted free cash flow of $80–$110 million.
Q3 guidance calls for net sales up 2–3%, gross margin of 44–45%, A&P spend of 15–16% of sales (the highest quarter of the year), and 40–45% of second-half EBITDA and EPS landing in Q3.
The Middle East conflict is expected to create $3–$5 million of incremental FY26 headwind (mostly margin), with potential FY27 impact roughly similar in size to the company's tariff exposure.
The Wet Shave manufacturing consolidation is on track to deliver savings beginning in FY27 with full run-rate in FY28, equating to roughly 200 bps of company-wide gross margin improvement.

Post-Fem Care divestiture (completed February), Wet Shave is ~60% of sales, Sun/Skin/Grooming combined approach 40% (Grooming over 10%), and the portfolio is roughly 50/50 North America/International.
Adjusted EBITDA was $73.8 million (vs. $84.7M prior year) and adjusted operating income was $49.4M or 9.5% of sales (vs. 12.8%), with A&P at 11.3% of sales versus 11.6% last year.

The company returned $23 million to shareholders in the quarter ($16M buybacks and $7M dividends at $0.15/share), used Fem Care proceeds to pay down the revolver, and expects FY26 adjusted net leverage of 3.3x–3.5x including a 0.3–0.4x temporary inflation from divestiture timing.
Q1 2026 consolidated revenues grew 12% year-over-year, AOP grew approximately 27% to $118 million, and AOP margin expanded 200 basis points to 16.6%.

Digital-only subscription revenues grew approximately 16% to $389 million, with 310,000 net new digital subscribers added, bringing the total subscriber base to over 13 million on the path to a 15 million milestone.
Digital advertising revenues grew approximately 32% to $93 million, exceeding guidance, while total advertising revenues increased about 17% to $127 million.
Digital-only ARPU grew 2.4%, driven by subscribers transitioning from promotional to higher prices and a bundled price increase.
Total subscription revenues grew 11.3% to approximately $517 million, above the company's prior guidance range.
Adjusted diluted EPS increased $0.20 year-over-year to $0.61, aided by a Q1 tax benefit from settled stock awards, with a normalized annual effective tax rate expected between 25% and 26%.

Q2 2026 guidance calls for digital-only subscription revenue growth of 14%–17%, digital advertising growth in the high teens, total advertising growth in high single digits, and adjusted operating costs up 8%–9%.

The company generated $542 million of free cash flow over the last 12 months and expects an approximately $60 million 2026 operating cash flow benefit from the One Big Beautiful Bill Act that is not expected to recur beyond fiscal 2026.
Affiliate, licensing and other revenues grew approximately 8% to $68.5 million, primarily from higher licensing revenues, with Q2 guidance for low single-digit growth.

The Times more than doubled production of reporter video in Q1 as part of a three-step video strategy (production, engagement, monetization), with management characterizing monetization as still early.
CareCloud raised full year 2025 revenue guidance to $117 million to $119 million, up from the prior guidance of $111 million to $114 million.
Q3 2025 revenue was $31.1 million, an increase of 9% from the same period last year.
Adjusted EBITDA increased 13% year-over-year to $7.7 million in Q3 2025.
The company generated $19.9 million of cash flow from operations for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, compared to $15.4 million in the same period last year.
CareCloud acquired Medsphere for $16.5 million, with approximately 70% of the purchase price funded from internally generated cash and no dilution to common shareholders.
The outstanding balance on the line of credit used for the Medsphere acquisition has been reduced to under $5 million, down from an initial draw of roughly half of the $16.5 million purchase price.
The Medsphere acquisition contributed approximately $3.4 million in revenue in Q3 2025 following its late August closing.
The company's Agentic AI front desk solution in pilot testing has successfully handled over 70% of incoming patient calls end-to-end without human intervention.
The AI front desk solution achieved over 80% success in appointment scheduling and related tasks during pilot deployments.
GAAP net income for the first nine months of 2025 was $7.9 million compared to $4.6 million for the same period in 2024, equating to income of $0.07 per share versus a $0.28 loss in the prior year.
Cirrus Logic reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $580.6 million, above the top end of guidance, driven by stronger-than-anticipated smartphone demand and favorable device mix.
The company achieved record non-GAAP earnings per share of $2.97 in the December quarter.
Non-GAAP gross margin was 53.1%, up 60 basis points sequentially due to reduced inventory reserves and supply chain efficiencies.
Cash and investments ended Q3 at $1.08 billion with no debt outstanding, up $185.9 million from the prior quarter.
Q3 non-GAAP free cash flow margin was 49%, with cash flow from operations of $290.8 million.
Q4 FY2026 revenue guidance is $410 million to $470 million, with non-GAAP operating expense expected at $124 million to $130 million.
The company's largest customer represented 94% of revenue in Q3, implying general market revenue declined significantly quarter-over-quarter.
Cirrus Logic repurchased approximately 591,000 shares for $70 million at an average price of $118.33, with $344.1 million remaining on the authorization.
PC revenue is expected to roughly double in FY26 from the low tens of millions in FY25, with SDCA programs growing from 19 in FY25 to over 60 in FY27.
The company estimates its automotive serviceable addressable market will be north of $800 million by 2029 across timing, audio, haptics, and telematics products.
Deere reported Q1 fiscal 2026 net sales and revenues up 13% to $9.611 billion, with equipment operations net sales up 18% to $8.001 billion, and net income of $656 million or $2.42 per diluted share.

Full year fiscal 2026 net income guidance was raised to between $4.5 billion and $5 billion, with equipment operations cash flow projections increased by $500 million at both ends to between $4.5 billion and $5.5 billion.
Total tariff costs for fiscal 2026 are projected at approximately $1.2 billion pretax, with IEEPA tariffs representing a little less than half of that total.

The Construction & Forestry order bank has risen by over 50% in the past quarter, reaching its highest point since May 2024, while Q1 retail settlements of construction and compact construction equipment were both up mid-teens year-over-year.
North American used Deere high-horsepower tractor inventory has declined over 10% from its March 2025 peak, with model year 2022 and 2023 8R tractors down more than 40% from that same period.
Nearly 99% of combines ordered through the early order program included some level of harvest automation, with nearly 80% taking the highest-level ultimate package, up 4 to 5 points year-over-year.

Small Ag & Turf net sales grew 24% year-over-year to $2.168 billion with a 9% operating margin, while current new field inventory for both tractor horsepower categories in this segment is approximately 40% lower year-over-year.

Construction & Forestry net sales forecast was raised to up approximately 15% for fiscal 2026 with an operating margin guide of 9% to 11%, supported by industry outlook increases to up around 5% for both construction and compact construction equipment in North America.
Deere's engaged acres increased over 10% from a year ago to 500 million, with highly engaged acres up approximately 25%, representing nearly one-third of total engaged acres.

Deere returned nearly $750 million in cash to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases during the quarter, and the company expects Production & Precision Ag to deliver double-digit operating margins in each remaining quarter of the fiscal year.

Q1 2026 Retail segment generated revenues of $1.4 billion, adjusted EBITDAR of $471.4 million, and margins of 33.2%, including a one-time $5 million legal accrual benefit primarily in the South region.
PENN raised the midpoint of 2026 Retail guidance by $20 million in revenue (to $5.73B-$5.86B) and $12 million in adjusted EBITDAR (to $1.88B-$1.98B).
Interactive segment Q1 adjusted EBITDA loss was $10.8 million, an approximately $78 million year-over-year improvement, with iCasino revenue up ~15% and OSB revenue up ~5%.
2026 Interactive guidance was revised to a $20 million adjusted EBITDA loss (vs. prior breakeven), entirely attributable to the Alberta launch on July 13, with Q4 expected to be profitable.
Management expects to delever by at least 1 full turn on lease-adjusted net leverage (to a midpoint ~5.5x, range 5.3-5.7x) and at least 2 full turns on traditional net leverage by year-end 2026.
Total 2026 CapEx guidance was reduced to $420 million from $445 million, with project CapEx cut to $200 million due to the Council Bluffs relocation timing shift to a 2028 opening.

PENN issued $600 million of unsecured notes due 2031 at 6.75% in March, ending Q1 with $1.7 billion in liquidity including $708 million in cash; cash interest expense is now projected at $150 million for 2026.

The company expects its 4 development projects (M Resort tower, Hollywood Joliet, Hollywood Columbus tower opening June 12, Hollywood Casino Aurora opening June 24) to generate 15%+ cash-on-cash returns on $800 million net project cost.
Jay Snowden stated PENN will generate $3+ of free cash flow per share in 2026, representing a ~20% free cash flow yield at the ~$15 share price, with the story expected to improve further in 2027.
Q1 OSB hold came in at 8.4% versus a structural hold of 9%, with approximately 60% of iCasino business sourced from OSB cross-sell; marketing spend was down over 65% year-over-year.

Q1 2026 core sales declined 3.5% and net sales declined 1.1%, both ahead of expectations, with all three segments exceeding plan and Learning & Development returning to core sales growth led by Baby's 4.9% growth.
Normalized EPS came in as a $0.05 loss, $0.03 better than the upper end of guidance, driven by higher core sales, better operating margin, and a 0% normalized effective tax rate in the quarter.

Newell raised its full-year 2026 outlook: net sales to flat-to-+2% (from -1% to +1%), core sales to -1% to +1% (from -2% to flat), and normalized diluted EPS to $0.56-$0.60 (from $0.54-$0.60), while maintaining normalized operating margin guidance of 8.6%-9.2%.

Q2 2026 guidance calls for both net and core sales to be flat to +2% (Newell's expected return to top-line growth), with normalized operating margin of 9.6%-10.2% and normalized diluted EPS of $0.16-$0.19.

Management identified approximately $50 million of incremental commodity/transportation inflation versus plan (about 60% from resin), with polyethylene expected to cost ~40% more for the balance of 2026 and diesel averaging ~$5/gallon.

Tariff-related P&L costs are now expected at $120 million ($0.24/share) for 2026 versus the original $146 million ($0.30/share), phased as $0.10 in Q1, $0.07 in Q2, $0.05 in Q3, and $0.03 in Q4, with tariff relief offsetting roughly half of the commodity headwind.
Newell plans to actively pursue refunds of approximately $120 million of IEEPA tariffs paid in 2025, but no benefit from these refunds is included in current earnings or cash flow guidance.

Q1 normalized gross margin expanded 70 bps to 33.2% and operating margin rose 30 bps to 4.8%, aided by a ~$25 million net pricing benefit from refined customer program estimates that added ~160 bps to core sales and ~110 bps to gross margin.

Net leverage stood at ~5.4x on net debt of $4.8 billion and trailing-12-month normalized EBITDA of $881 million, with plans to reduce year-end leverage by about half a turn; operating cash flow guidance of $350-$400 million was maintained but is now expected toward the low end.

China-sourced finished goods have been reduced from a peak of ~35% of global COGS to under 10%, and Newell plans to launch 25 Tier 1/Tier 2 innovations in 2026 (up from 18 in 2025), with 6 of the top 10 U.S. brands gaining market share in Q1.
Q3 FY2026 results delivered 7% revenue growth, 80 basis points of adjusted EBIT margin expansion, and 10% adjusted EPS growth, all ahead of expectations.

ADP raised full-year FY2026 guidance to 6%-7% consolidated revenue growth, 70-80 bps of adjusted EBIT margin expansion, and 10%-11% adjusted EPS growth, while maintaining the 4%-7% ES new business bookings range.
Employer Services retention guidance improved by 10 bps to flat-to-down 20 bps for the year, with both ES retention and overall client satisfaction reaching new Q3 record highs.
ES segment revenue grew 7% reported (5% organic constant currency) with ~1.5+ points of FX benefit expected to moderate in Q4, and ES margins expanded 130 bps in the quarter.
Client funds interest revenue guidance was raised by $25 million at the midpoint to $1.34-$1.35 billion, driven by 9% growth in average client funds balances and an unchanged ~3.4% average yield.
Pricing contribution to revenue is now expected at ~130 bps versus the prior ~100 bps target, reflecting value-based pricing power alongside record retention and satisfaction.

PEO total revenue grew 7% (5% ex-pass-throughs) with 2% worksite employee growth, but PEO margins fell 120 bps due to zero-margin pass-throughs, higher SUI costs, higher selling expenses from strong bookings, and lower workers' comp reserve releases.

Share repurchase activity has been meaningfully elevated this fiscal year, and management expects to continue buybacks at or above these elevated levels through the rest of FY2026 and throughout FY2027.

AI deployment is driving tangible productivity: ADP Assist payroll agents save ~30 minutes per payroll, Smart Actions reduced clicks/time by ~80%, RUN client contacts fell 8% YoY in Q3, and India year-end AI deployment cut call volumes and labor by 35%.

Zone GenAI service platform reached 20% of the service population in March with expectations of over 40% by end of FY2026, and management expects FY2027 reinvestment yields on the client funds portfolio to exceed FY2026 levels, supporting continued margin acceleration.
Balchem reported record quarterly consolidated revenue of $268 million, an increase of 11.5% compared to the prior year quarter.
The company achieved its 25th consecutive quarter of year-over-year growth in adjusted EBITDA.
Record quarterly adjusted EBITDA was $71 million, an increase of 11% compared to the prior year, with an adjusted EBITDA margin rate of 26.7%.
Adjusted earnings per diluted share were $1.35, up $0.22 or 19.5% compared to the prior year.
Human Nutrition & Health segment generated record sales of $174 million, an increase of 14.3% from the prior year, with the Nutrient Portfolio up about 30% and Food Ingredients up almost 7%.
Net debt decreased to $89 million with an overall leverage ratio on a net debt basis of 0.3x.
Free cash flow was $51 million for the quarter, with $65 million of cash on the balance sheet.
The encapsulates business grew approximately 26% in Q3, and a new Orange County facility with twice the current capacity is expected to begin production by mid-2027.
Animal Nutrition & Health segment sales were $56 million, up 6.6% from prior year, while Specialty Products segment sales were $36 million, up 7.5%.
The company stated it has fully offset the impact of tariffs through alternate supply chain options or subsequent pricing actions and expects to similarly offset any future tariff impacts.
MannKind delivered record quarterly revenue of $82 million in Q3 2025, representing 17% growth over the prior year.
Tyvaso DPI generated $33 million in royalties (up 23% year-over-year) and $26 million in manufacturing-related revenue in Q3 2025.
FUROSCIX dispensed over 27,000 doses in Q3 2025, up 153% from the same quarter last year, with year-to-date revenue of $47.1 million (95% increase over 2024).
MannKind used $133 million of its $286 million cash and investments and borrowed $325 million from Blackstone to fund the scPharmaceuticals acquisition.
Afrezza net revenue rose 23% to $18.5 million in Q3 2025, with new prescriptions up 31% and total prescriptions up 27% year-over-year.
Non-GAAP net income increased to $22.4 million in Q3 2025, up from $15.4 million in Q3 2024, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.07 versus $0.06 in the prior year.
Afrezza units per prescription declined approximately 15% year-over-year due to the shift in focus toward type 1 diabetes patients who require less insulin than type 2 patients.
The company achieved its interim enrollment target ahead of schedule in the ICoN-1 global Phase III NTM study and expects to confirm trial sizing mid-2026.

In preclinical DIO studies, nimacimab monotherapy produced approximately 14% vehicle-adjusted weight loss, while the APC arm and the mixed combination arm both produced additive weight loss beyond the 21-23% seen with GLP-1 agonists alone.
